title: Parcel budget: Proof strip
topics: Greedy choices, dynamic programming and backtracking
summary: Each parcel is [weight,value], with positive weight and nonnegative value. For every capacity from 0 through k, produce the maximum total value obtainable by choosing each parcel at most once and using no more than that capacity. Return the entire derived sequence, preserving its order.
descriptionMd:
Each office parcel may be selected once while a packing clerk compares all capacities through k. Luz rolls a fresh proof strip into the office typewriter. The supervisor wants the readings in their precise working order before signing the file.

Each parcel is [weight,value], with positive weight and nonnegative value. For every capacity from 0 through k, produce the maximum total value obtainable by choosing each parcel at most once and using no more than that capacity.

Return the entire derived sequence, preserving its order.

Implement parcelBudgetProofStrip(drawers, k). Use k exactly where specified above.
unitIntro: Zero-one knapsack. Each parcel is [weight,value], with positive weight and nonnegative value. For every capacity from 0 through k, produce the maximum total value obtainable by choosing each parcel at most once and using no more than that capacity. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n*k); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(k). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with zero-one knapsack. What state describes the portion you have already processed?
